The '''Nexus Tools Platform''' or '''NTP''' is a web-based inventory platform that allows an interactive comparison of [[Integrated assessment modelling|environmental models]] in a [[Statistics|statistical]] way. Developed by the [[UNU-FLORES|UNU Institute for Integrated Management of Material Fluxes and of Resources (UNU-FLORES)]],<ref name="NTP paper" /> the platform helps a user to analyze existing modelling tools related to [[environmental resource management]] and associated nexus perspectives, such as a [[Water, energy and food security nexus|Water-Energy-Food Nexus]]. As a result, the user can select the most appropriate tools to fit the research needs.

==Integrated Resources Management (Nexus Approach)==
Considering an increase in the [[World population|global population]], the demand for both [[food]] and [[water]] is expected to grow by more than 50% by 2050.<ref name="Food Demand">{{cite journal |last1=Valin  |first1=H. |last2=et |first2=al |date=2014 |title=The future of food demand: understanding differences in global economic models |journal=Agricultural Economics |volume=45 |pages=51–67 |doi=10.1111/agec.12089|hdl=10568/52170 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref name="OECD">{{cite web|title=OECD ENVIRONMENTAL OUTLOOK TO 2050: The Consequences of Inaction. Key Facts and Figures  |url=http://www.oecd.org/env/indicators-modelling-outlooks/49910023.pdf |publisher=OECD|date=2012|access-date=13 March 2019}}</ref>
At the same time, [[Agriculture|agricultural]] activity already puts significant stress on the quantity and quality of [[soil]]s and [[List of countries by freshwater withdrawal|freshwater resources]] worldwide. This leads to growing rates of [[land degradation]]<ref name="Erosion">{{cite journal |last1=Borrelli |first1=Pasquale |last2=et |first2=al |date=2017 |title=An Assessment of the Global Impact of 21st Century Land Use Change on Soil Erosion |journal=Nature Communications |volume=8 |doi=10.1038/s41467-017-02142-7 |doi-access=free|pmc=5722879 |pmid=29222506 }}</ref> and [[ecosystem]] deterioration.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sánchez-Bayo|first1=Francisco |last2=Wyckhuys|first2=Kris A.G. |date=2019 |title=Worldwide decline of the entomofauna: A review of its drivers |journal=Biological Conservation |volume=232 |pages=8–27 |doi=10.1016/j.biocon.2019.01.020|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Long-term solutions to those challenges require integrated [[Environmental resource management|management of environmental resources]] which can be also referred to as a [https://flores.unu.edu/en/research/nexus Nexus Approach].
This approach focuses on the [[Synergy|synergies]] between sectors in order to minimize [[trade-off]]s, increase [[Resource efficiency|resource use efficiency]], and improve environmental [[Environmental policy|policy]] & [[Environmental governance|governance]] which is crucial for the achievement of the [[Sustainable Development Goals]].

For example, the sustainable management of [[wastewater]] in [[Crop|crop production]] is considered as an implementation of a ''Water-Soil-Waste Nexus''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Hettiarachchi |first1=Hiroshan |last2=Ardakanian |first2=Reza |date=2016 |title=Safe Use of Wastewater in Agriculture: Good Practice Examples |url=https://collections.unu.edu/eserv/UNU:5764/SafeUseOfWastewaterInAgriculture.pdf |location=Dresden |publisher=UNU-FLORES |isbn=978-3-944863-31-3 }}</ref>

==Mission==
Integrated [[Environmental resource management|resource management]] requires the use of [[Integrated assessment modelling|integrated environmental modelling]] tools. However, there is no single [[Mathematical model|model]] that can cover all complex interactions between natural resources such as [[water]], [[soil]], and [[waste]].<ref name="NTP paper" /> Moreover, there is a poor awareness of the available models and their capabilities which results in a time-consuming process of developing new models instead of using or further expanding already existing ones.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nexus Tools Platform: An Interactive Platform for Inter-model Comparison of Existing Modelling Tools |url=https://www.water-energy-food.org/resources/resources-detail/tools-nexus-tools-platform-an-interactive-platform-for-inter-model-comparison-of-existing-modelling-tools |publisher=Nexus - The Water, Energy & Food Security Platform|date=2018|access-date=24 April 2019}}</ref>

With the objective of addressing the abovementioned problems, the [http://data.flores.unu.edu/projects/ntp Nexus Tools Platform] has been created. It provides detailed visualizations of model descriptions and advanced filtering options using [[Kibana]] [[Open source|open-source]] visualization software. The platform does not attempt to include all possible models, but rather to provide a more efficient way to compare well-established ones and to keep the content updated through the feedback system with model users and [[Software developer|developers]].

[[File:NTP screenshot.jpg|400px|thumb|center|The screenshot of the Nexus Tools Platform visualization (March 2019)]]

==History==
The first version of the website was published in April 2015 starting with the [[database]] of 60 models from around the world.<ref name="NTP release">{{cite web|title=UNU Launches Interactive Platform for Comparing Nexus-Related Modeling Tools |url=http://sdg.iisd.org/news/unu-launches-interactive-platform-for-comparing-nexus-related-modeling-tools |publisher=International Institute for Sustainable Development|date=2015|access-date=24 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=UNU-FLORES Launches Nexus Tools Platform |url=https://unu.edu/news/news/unu-flores-launches-nexus-tools-platform.html |publisher=UNU-FLORES|date=2015|access-date=13 March 2019}}</ref> A year later, a paper was published in [[Environmental Modelling & Software]] journal explaining the NTP development, [[data collection]] methodology, and application examples.<ref name="NTP paper">{{cite journal |last1=Mannschatz |first1=T. |last2=et |first2=al |date=2016 |title=Nexus Tools Platform: Web-Based Comparison of Modelling Tools for Analysis of Water-Soil-Waste Nexus |journal=Environmental Modelling & Software |volume=76 |pages=137–53 |doi=10.1016/j.envsoft.2015.10.031}}</ref> In March 2018, NTP 2.0 was released with a greater number of available models (84), improved classification and visualization.<ref>{{cite web|title=5 Things You Need to Know about Nexus Tools Platform 2.0 |url=https://flores.unu.edu/en/news/news/5-things-you-need-to-know-about-nexus-tools-platform-2-0.html |publisher=UNU-FLORES|date=2018|access-date=24 April 2019}}</ref> Through the advanced search and filter functions, users could differentiate modelling tools in terms of model types, popularity, considered processes, input and output parameters, application areas (countries), programming language, etc. Recently, the whole database was refreshed and one more model was added making 85 in total.

==Data Sources==
The data for the platform is collected in two ways:
* The [[open access]] information which is available on the respective model [[websites]], [[User guide|manuals]], and [[publications]]. This information is further processed to fit the NTP [[classification]] system;
* The information provided directly by the model [[Software developer|developers]].

The current list of models includes a wide array of research areas from [[hydrology]] and [[land management]] to [[soil]] and [[water quality]] topics from a local to global scale. Some of the most popular examples are [[SWAT model|SWAT]], [[MODFLOW]], [[HEC-RAS]], and [[CESM]].

The NTP is not intended to promote any of the models listed on the website. The information, whether in graphical or text form, is presented for scientific and educational purposes only.
